prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
answers:
[goal] One regex in `./regex.txt` that, per line containing a valid IPv4 address, yields the last valid calendar date on that line via `re.findall(pattern, text, re.MULTILINE)`.

[action] Wrote `regex.txt` (484 chars, single line, exactly one capture group) built from three parts:
- Line gate: `^(?=[^\n]*<IP>)` so lines without an address produce nothing.
- Last-date capture: `[^\n]*?(<DATE>)(?![^\n]*<DATE>)` (first date with no later valid date on the line = the last one).
- `<IP>`: octet `25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9]` repeated 4x with `(?<![0-9A-Za-z])` / `(?![0-9A-Za-z])` guards; `<DATE>`: `[0-9]{4}-` plus month/day alternations (31-day, 30-day, `02-(0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])`) with the same guards.

Assumptions I chose: year is any 4 digits, no leap-year rule (Feb 29 always valid, per brief); "right before/after" means an ASCII letter or digit, so punctuation like `(10.0.0.1)` or `2026-04-30,` still counts and `_` does not block; "last date" means last *valid* date, so a trailing `2026-02-30` is ignored rather than suppressing the line; a line with an address but no valid date yields nothing; `re.findall` returns the single capture group, the date.

[result] Verified two ways. 33 hand cases pass (invalid dates `2026-02-30`/`2026-13-01`/`2026-04-31`, adjacency `x2026-04-30`, `2026-04-301`, `a10.0.0.1`, `256.0.0.1`, `10.0.0.01`, `1.2.3.4.5`, multi-IP/multi-date ordering). Then a 60,000-line fuzz against an independent Python reference scanner: `fuzz fails: 0`. On the provided `server.log` it returns `['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']`, matching the three address-bearing lines and their last dates (lines 2 and 4 correctly produce nothing). Compile check: 1 group, 0 newlines in the file.

[next] Nothing open. If real logs ever need leap-year-strict February or reject punctuation-adjacent tokens, the guards and the `02-` branch are the only spots to change. No browser or app windows were opened.
